batches.evidence: Independent source review found a lazy OnceLock initializer can still recover journals and spawn workers after quit captured a missing service. It also found terminal journal-write failure can leave a persisted active state after the real worker has ended. Original requests and startup/reset contracts reread; accessible thread inventory rechecked and complete source snapshot hashes unchanged.
batches.decision: Register lazy initialization under the existing admission gate with an RAII count, without holding that mutex across I/O. Quit/reset drain waits for admitted initialization before obtaining the final service. Updates see initialization as active work. Separately track actual media work ownership and record terminal persistence errors. Once all workers have really stopped, an ordinary requested quit may preserve the last valid journal and originals for recovery and exit with a diagnostic warning; factory reset must reject that persistence error before publishing its marker. Never infer completed output, cleanup permission, or terminated workers from a timeout.
checks: Quit/update reservation rejects late initialization
Slow initialization does not hold the UI admission mutex
Initializers are counted through completion and panic, and drain rereads the service after waiting
Terminal persistence failure cannot make actual worker drain infinite
Factory reset does not publish a marker when drained work reports persistence failure
All tests use isolated fixtures, not real reset or user media
